content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or corrections.
- Overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum or mean reversion.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in downward trends — forecasts dip too early or too late.
- Overreacts to recent volatility: after a spike, model overshoots in the immediate next few days, then corrects too slowly.
- Underestimates mean reversion in the final 10 days — fails to recognize that prices often return to prior levels after a sharp move.
- Shows persistent bias toward lower values in the first 10 days of the forecast, especially when history shows strong upward momentum.
- When true values are above 70, model often underestimates the peak and fails to capture the full magnitude of the rally.
- When true values are below 60, model tends to overestimate — especially in the first 5 days — possibly due to ignoring recent downward momentum.
